newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs close up sharply, Aug bellies up limit.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs close up sharply, Aug bellies up limit.

text.p: CME lean hog futures held sharp gains and August pork belly futures ended up the daily 3.000 cent per lb limit on demand linked to stronger cash market expectations, traders said.
Hogs closed 1.525 to 0.150 cent higher with August up 0.575 at 81.925 cents. Pork bellies ended up limit up of 3.000 to 0.550 cents with August limit up at 86.200 cents.
Hog futures rose as recently-reduced slaughter rates were expected to bolster wholesale pork prices next week and stimulate increased packer demand for cash hogs going into next week, traders said.

"It looks like the packers intend to keep their market share so they continue to be underneath the market giving us some support on the cash and the futures," said Don Roose, President of U.S. Commodities Inc.
Cash hogs are now called steady-firm Friday and prices could rise $1 or more by early next week. Values could move even higher if packers become very competitive, sources said.
Roose, along with other traders, also cited the Japanese tariff situation as supportive.

Japan has said it will drop its tariff on imported pork in August to help bring down pork prices for Japanese consumers. Speculation has circulated in the market this week that Japan my extend that move beyond August.
"Their inventory ran low and they are trying to replenish and they are going to replenish the easiest way they can, Roose said of Japan's pork inventories.

Refco sold late which limited gains, traders said. Rand Financials and Cargill Investor Services notably bought on the advance with buy stops adding to gains in October above 75.000 cents, pit sources said.
In hog options, commission houses sold October 74 and 76 calls early and a couple of houses sold the August 81.950 synthetic and bought the October 75.400 futures late, pit sources added.
August pork bellies moved limit up by midsession and held there at the close on between 25 and 50 unfilled buy stops with the August option synthetic ended up at 87.000 cents, sources said.

Cash belly prices were seen rising on brisk user demand for the recently reduced supplies, sources said. They estimated cash bellies could rise to $92 to $94 per cwt from the current $90 level, basis the 14- to 16-lb weight group, traders said.
